intent: Test whether the iteration 5 geometry with wheel_track narrowed to 0.09 m (from 0.10 m) adds enough yaw to clear the s-bend drift at max_error about 0.061 to 0.062 m, while keeping the proven ±0.06 m sensor row. This isolates the track change, because iteration 7 and 8 confounded it with the widened row. Expected: s-bend progress at or above 0.42 and max_error at or below 0.061 m; oval finish at least 0.85. Fallback if the oval fails: return wheel_track to 0.10 m, the known-good iteration 5 geometry.
learning: Iteration 9's race output matched iteration 8 exactly while its produced geometry matched iteration 5, so the race may have run a stale design. Ask the Integrator to confirm which geometry was loaded in iteration 9. Also ask whether the oval finish returns to about 1.0 with ±0.06 m, since that would show the row width caused the iteration 7 and 8 collapses. On the s-bend, ask whether max_error is reached on the first or second bend, and whether the outer sensors read near zero at the drift point.
rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 5 is the best design so far (386.35): wheel_track 0.10 m, five sensors at y=0.08 spanning x=±0.06, 12 mm footprints. It gave 20 of 20 oval finishes and s-bend progress 0.42. Narrowing the track from 0.12 to 0.10 m moved s-bend progress from 0.17 to 0.42, so turn rate per unit of steering is the s-bend lever. Iteration 6 (16 mm footprint) cut the oval finish to 0.55 and did not fix the slalom, so footprint is rejected. Iterations 7 and 8 both widened the row to ±0.07 m. Their oval finish fell to 0.15 at 0.09 m and to 0.45 at 0.10 m, so the widened row is the likely cause of the oval loss, and the track alone does not explain it.

Iteration 9 needs a flag. Its produced geometry matches iteration 5 (±0.06, 0.10 m), but its race result matches iteration 8 (±0.07 row) to four decimal places. The race may have run a stale design, so I cannot treat iteration 9 as a clean test of the ±0.06 row. I therefore do not read iteration 9 as evidence for or against ±0.06 at 0.10 m.

Decision. Keep the proven ±0.06 m row and 12 mm footprint. Change one variable: wheel_track 0.10 to 0.09 m. This is the turn-rate lever the s-bend evidence points to, and it isolates the track change from the row change that broke the oval in iterations 7 and 8. Body, wheels and mass stay the same. The off-track floor binds at 0.06 m for every body width, so body changes are not useful. Expected result: s-bend progress at or above 0.42 with max_error at or below 0.061 m, oval finish at least 0.85. If the oval finish falls below 0.85 or steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.3, revert to 0.10 m in iteration 11, which is the known-good geometry. Slalom line loss (about one per run at progress 0.10) is still open. I will not change sensing for it until the track result is known.
